notes: The italic *oppressed they* is the second realization of the written רָצַץ, which the Hebrew does write in this coordination, so both realizations are one discontinuous unit headed on the first (rules 34, 25); the competing `added` reading under rule 20 is named in the unit note, and the italics decide nothing (rule 7).
*that year* is written as a bare accusative, so the בְּ is unrepresented (rule 40) while the demonstrative pronoun takes the phrase's single determiner and both articles are unrepresented (rule 41).
בְּעֵבֶר fuses to *beyond* under rule 30, the verbless clause's copula joining that one unit without defeating the one-rendering condition.
In *the land of the Amorites* the ASV writes a *the* before each word, so nothing is fronted: the article takes the one before its own word and the construct a supplied one (rule 29).
